issues.failure_explanation: The weighted condition in Definition def:weight uses the parameter integral ds, not arclength. Replacing a parametrization by its constant-speed reparametrization changes this integral unless the original speed is already proportional to arclength, so the claimed exact equivalence is false.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, $t$-design curves are exactly curves which, when reparametrized to have constant speed, are weighted $t$-design curves.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Clarify that an unweighted t-design curve corresponds to the constant-speed parametrization of a curve whose arclength integral averages polynomials, and that the weighted property is parametrization-dependent.
issues.overall_effect: The background identification of unweighted and weighted t-design curves is unreliable, and any inference treating arbitrary weighted parametrizations as reparametrizations of unweighted design curves is unsupported.
issues.title: False equivalence between unweighted and weighted t-design curves under constant-speed reparametrization

issues.failure_explanation: The proof replaces the integral over S^d by (1/2) times the integral over s of normalized fiber averages. This disintegration is correct only when the marginal distribution of h(ω)=ω_1 is uniform, which happens for S^2 but not for general S^d. For f(ω)=ω_1^2 the displayed calculation gives 1/3, while the sphere average is 1/(d+1), so the equality fails for d≠2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must reparameterize the lift or reweight the intervals so that the induced s-distribution matches the latitude density of S^d, and reprove the design identity.
issues.overall_effect: The central construction lifting weighted t-design sets on S^{d-1} to weighted t-design curves on S^d is false as proved for d>2, undermining the weighted existence results in those dimensions.
issues.title: Weighted lifting theorem uses incorrect sphere disintegration for d>2
issues.why_classification: Every supported resolution either excludes all d>2 or requires a new nontrivial construction/argument for the weighted lift; the advertised all-d weighted result does not survive as written.

issues.failure_explanation: W_t is twice the total length of a minimal spanning tree for Y_t. The source gives no argument that this total length is bounded by (|Y_t|-1)ρ_t/4 from a covering radius; Proposition pro:covrad establishes a nearest-neighbor distance, not an edge-length bound for the chosen tree. Consequently the derived W_t≲t^{2n-1} is unsupported, and even if the upper bound were true it only yields ε_t≲1/t, not the stated two-sided ε_t≍1/t.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove a uniform upper bound on the total length of the chosen spanning tree for the t-design sets used, and either prove a matching lower bound or weaken the statement to ε_t=O(1/t).
issues.overall_effect: The main approximate odd-sphere theorem's advertised error rate is not established, and the dependent even-sphere and Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund consequences are unreliable.
issues.title: Main approximate theorem relies on an unsupported bound for W_t and proves at most O(1/t) error
issues.why_classification: The central rate guarantee depends on a missing nontrivial geometric estimate; no comparable source-supported repair preserving the stated two-sided rate is available.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=0 the statement asks for simple approximate t-design curves on S^0 with length asymptotic to t^{-3}. A continuous map from the connected interval [0,1] to the two-point discrete sphere S^0 is constant, so the required positive length asymptotic and design property cannot hold as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the theorem to n≥1 (equivalently d≥2), or provide a separate valid low-dimensional construction if S^0 is intended.
issues.overall_effect: The even-sphere theorem includes a degenerate dimension that is not valid.
